objections.claim: The pinned slug rule is not the codebase's existing slug convention, and the spec never establishes that the consumer will adopt it: FAFF-930's assembler does not exist and is out of scope, so the producer-side field's only consumer is a future, unspecified component and the join-key rule is only half-pinned.
objections.evidence: Spec §1 one-derivation-rule principle; §2 Out of scope; §4 Slug discipline (no cap, no fallback vs adr.js/decisions.js/prd.js); §6 (assembler does not exist).
objections.predicted_consequence: When FAFF-930 lands its author either re-derives slugs with a different convention and the producer's anchors zero-match en masse, or is forced to import heading-slug.js and special-case an uncapped slug no other part of the repo produces — either way the binding the ticket sells is not guaranteed by anything that ships in this change.

objections.claim: The LLM producer cannot execute the pinned rule, so the pinned-on-both-sides guarantee is weaker than stated: the unit test proves only the code side, and the only drift signal lives in out-of-scope FAFF-930.
objections.evidence: Spec §4 (producers are LLMs; they cannot call code); §4 Failure modes; §4 unit-test pin.
objections.predicted_consequence: The ticket ships green on every gate it names while delivering a spec_anchor that may be frequently wrong or absent in practice, with no in-repo signal that the binding actually binds.

objections.claim: The identical-derivation-rule requirement across six prose files has no mechanical check: validate-adapters checks line caps, not content identity, so the identical-wording invariant is a human-review criterion with no oracle.
objections.predicted_consequence: A build could ship with two paraphrases of the rule that a refuter reads differently for an edge heading, passing every named gate; the two-homes-cannot-drift invariant holds only for the code home.
